request: Analyze GSE302911 for PMID 40623475 (Endurance training promotes chromatin closure and timely repression of the post-exercise immediate early stress response.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq, M. quadriceps, Illumina NovaSeq 6000, STAR + salmon, TPM matrix (S2.8.p1)
final.organism: Mouse, male C57BL/6 WT, 22-26 weeks at sacrifice (S2.1.p1)
final.groups: 7 groups x n=3: sedentary; untrained 0h/6h/72h; trained 0h/6h/72h (S2.3.p1, GEO treatment column)
final.primary_estimand: Bulk-muscle gene expression change in each exercised condition (untrained or trained, 0h/6h/72h after an exhaustive treadmill bout) versus sedentary baseline
planned_contrasts: untrained 0h vs sedentary (FIG4 A; count shown only in figure, myonuclear subset)
final.inclusion: all 21 samples; DEG counts in FIG4 A restricted to the ATAC-derived myonuclear gene subset (23% of genes, S3.4.p1), which needs GSE302910 peak calls and is not reproduced
final.paper_method: DESeq2 (GEO data_processing: Differential expression analysis was performed with DESeq2 v3.16); input stated as salmon TPM collected into a count matrix (S2.8.p1)
final.paper_results: 1,848 myonuclear-subset genes up/down in >=1 condition (S3.4.p1); more up/down at 0h trained vs untrained, similar up at 6h, more down in trained at 6h, very few changes at 72h (S3.4.p1); Klf5 and Esrrg show training-state-dependent expression (S3.4.p1, FIG4 C)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.3.p1 defines 12-week wheel training then one exhaustive bout with sacrifice at 0h/6h/72h; S3.4.p1 and FIG4 define RNA-seq DEGs as each condition versus sedentary at |log2FC| 0.585 and FDR<0.05; S2.8.p1 states salmon TPM; GEO data_processing names DESeq2. Per-contrast DEG counts exist only in Figure 4A bars and only for the myonuclear subset, so no numeric paper count is available for a genome-wide comparison.

exclude_samples.GSM9113529: Trained_0h_1 column is byte-identical to Untrained_0h_1; excluded with its twin because the duplicated profile cannot belong to both groups

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns were renamed by name rule (prep_matrix.py inserts the underscore before the replicate digit, checked against GEO library names) and matched exactly to the Library name token in GEO description. Group from GEO characteristics treatment. Duplicate-column check found Untrained_0h1 == Trained_0h1 exactly (25,037 shared non-zero values, equal library sums 997,304); both copies excluded.

matrix.reasoning: File name says TPM; S2.8.p1 says TPM values were collected; column sums are ~997,300-997,900 (TPM sums to 1e6 before gene filtering) and values are non-integer. No raw or estimated counts are deposited, so count methods are not valid.

final.analysis_type: multi-group, one control (sedentary) with six exercised conditions; one model

candidates.reason_rejected: sedentary has no time level and is neither trained nor exercised; the paper compares every condition to sedentary (FIG4)
pools distinct levels; paper reports per-condition contrasts

design.reasoning: FIG4 A/B and S3.4.p1: each exercised condition versus sedentary. One model on all samples with six planned contrasts; other pairwise comparisons (e.g. trained vs untrained at a time point) are exploratory. Trained-vs-sedentary contrasts combine 12-week training and the acute bout, as in the paper.

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, one sample per mouse; no batch, lane or sex variation recorded (all male, S2.1.p1).

final.method: limma (moderated t, empirical Bayes) on log2(TPM+1)

paper_route.reason: only a TPM matrix is deposited (supplementary file NONE per sample); DESeq2 requires raw counts and TPM must not be rounded to integers

deviations: limma on log2(TPM+1) instead of DESeq2
two duplicated 0h samples excluded (0h groups n=2)

method.reasoning: Matrix policy: TPM -> log2(x+1) -> limma. Paper's DESeq2 route blocked by missing counts; declared deviation.

final.deviation_note: same BH FDR and |log2FC| rule applied to limma statistics instead of DESeq2; BH applied within each contrast

threshold.reasoning: FIG4 legend: log2 fold change +/- 0.585, FDR <0.05. The paper states the log2 cutoff directly (0.585), so it is used as written rather than log2(1.5)=0.5849625.

final.exploratory_reason: grp_U0_vs_SED and grp_T0_vs_SED have n=2 in the exercised arm after excluding the duplicated library; training_state contrasts (T vs U per time point) are not tested in the paper and T0_vs_U0 is 2 vs 2
caveats: paper DEG counts (FIG4 A) are restricted to an ATAC-derived myonuclear subset and given only as bars, so our genome-wide counts are not directly comparable
trained-vs-sedentary contrasts confound training and acute exercise by design

study.reasoning: Declared deviation (limma on log2 TPM). Paper names Klf5 and Esrrg as training-state-dependent exercise genes (S3.4.p1, FIG4 C) and immediate early genes Fos, Jun, Atf3, Egr1, Nr4a family (S3.5.p1, motif level).

executions.reasoning: Same cell-means limma model; trained vs untrained at each post-exercise time point addresses the paper's training-state question directly (S3.4.p1) but is not a tested contrast in the paper, so exploratory.
